subject: ela
intro: When you meet a word you do not know, you do not have to stop reading. You can be a word detective. Look for context clues, the other words in the sentence that hint at the meaning. Look at word parts: a prefix at the front (un-, re-, pre-), a suffix at the end (-ful, -less, -able), or a root word you already know. If clues are not enough, a glossary or dictionary gives the meaning. In this lesson you will practice each strategy so you can figure out new and multiple-meaning words on your own.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to find the meaning of the underlined word.

The soup was so bland that Dad added salt, pepper, and garlic to give it more flavor.

What does "bland" most likely mean?

steps: Look at the words around "bland" for clues.
Dad added salt, pepper, and garlic "to give it more flavor."
If he needed to add flavor, the soup did not have much flavor to start.
So "bland" means having little or no flavor.
solution.answer: "Bland" means not having much taste or flavor. The clue is that Dad added seasonings "to give it more flavor."

items.prompt:
Use the prefix to find the meaning of the underlined word.

The scarf was so tangled that it took Maria ten minutes to untangle it.

What does "untangle" mean, and how does the prefix help?

steps: Break the word into parts: un- + tangle.
The prefix un- means "the opposite of" or "to undo."
So "untangle" means to undo the tangles.
The sentence fits: the scarf was tangled, so she worked to undo it.
solution.answer: "Untangle" means to take the tangles out, or to undo a tangle. The prefix un- means "undo," so untangle is the opposite of tangle.

items.prompt:
Use the suffix to find the meaning of the underlined word.

After the long hike with no water, the travelers were helpless without a map or a phone.

What does "helpless" mean, and how does the suffix help?

steps: Break the word into parts: help + -less.
The suffix -less means "without."
So "helpless" means without help, or not able to help yourself.
The sentence fits: they had no map or phone, so they could not help themselves.
solution.answer: "Helpless" means without help or unable to help yourself. The suffix -less means "without," so helpless is being without help.

items.prompt:
This word has two meanings. Use context clues to choose the right one.

The baseball player swung the bat as hard as he could.

What does "bat" mean in this sentence?

steps: "Bat" can mean a flying animal or a stick used in a sport.
The sentence talks about a baseball player who "swung" it.
You swing a wooden or metal bat in baseball, not an animal.
So here "bat" means the stick used to hit a baseball.
solution.answer: Here "bat" means the wooden or metal stick used to hit a baseball. The clues "baseball player" and "swung" point to the sports meaning, not the animal.

items.prompt:
Use context clues to find the meaning of the underlined word.

The puppy was timid at first and hid behind the couch, but soon it felt brave enough to come say hello.

What does "timid" most likely mean?

steps: Look for clues around "timid."
The puppy "hid behind the couch" at first.
Later it felt "brave," which is the opposite.
So "timid" means shy or fearful.
solution.answer: "Timid" means shy or easily scared. The clue is that the puppy hid at first, before it felt brave.

items.prompt:
Use the prefix to find the meaning of the underlined word.

Before the big game, the coach asked the team to preview the plays one more time so nothing would surprise them.

What does "preview" mean, and how does the prefix help?

steps: Break the word into parts: pre- + view.
The prefix pre- means "before."
"View" means to look at or see.
So "preview" means to look at something before, ahead of time.
solution.answer: "Preview" means to look at something ahead of time, before it fully happens. The prefix pre- means "before," so preview is to view beforehand.

items.prompt:
Use the suffix to find the meaning of the underlined word.

The blanket was so colorful, with red, blue, yellow, and green stripes, that everyone noticed it.

What does "colorful" mean, and how does the suffix help?

steps: Break the word into parts: color + -ful.
The suffix -ful means "full of."
So "colorful" means full of color.
The sentence fits: the blanket had many colors, red, blue, yellow, and green.
solution.answer: "Colorful" means full of color, having many colors. The suffix -ful means "full of," so colorful is full of color.

items.prompt:
Use the root word to find the meaning of the underlined word.

The old bridge was unsafe, so the city closed it until workers could fix it.

What does "unsafe" mean, and how do the word parts help?

steps: Break the word into parts: un- + safe.
The root word is "safe."
The prefix un- means "not."
So "unsafe" means not safe, which is why the city closed the bridge.
solution.answer: "Unsafe" means not safe, or dangerous. The root word is "safe" and the prefix un- means "not," so unsafe is the opposite of safe.

items.prompt:
This word has two meanings. Use context clues to choose the right one.

Mom used a ruler to draw a straight line across the page.

What does "ruler" mean in this sentence?

steps: "Ruler" can mean a king or queen who rules, or a straight tool for measuring and drawing.
The sentence says Mom used it "to draw a straight line."
You draw a straight line with the measuring tool, not with a king.
So here "ruler" means the measuring tool.
solution.answer: Here "ruler" means the flat, straight tool used to measure and draw straight lines. The clue "to draw a straight line" points to the tool, not a king or queen.

items.prompt:
You read this sentence and are still not sure of the word.

The scientist studied the nocturnal owl, which only comes out at night.

Explain how you would find the meaning of "nocturnal," then give the meaning.

steps: First try context clues: the sentence says the owl "only comes out at night."
That hints "nocturnal" is about nighttime.
If you want to be sure, look it up in a glossary or dictionary.
Both the clue and the dictionary agree on the meaning.
solution.answer: "Nocturnal" means active at night. You can use the context clue "only comes out at night," and check a glossary or dictionary to be sure.
